evals.prompt: Where did we leave triage last week? Show me everything Pix is tracking.
evals.expected_output: A read-only dashboard from `.vulnetix/memory.yaml` with a summary header, open-vuln table sorted by CWSS, resolved-vuln table, and manifest tracking.
expectations: `.vulnetix/memory.yaml` is loaded via the Read tool (after a Glob existence check)
Summary header `Open: <N>` and `Resolved: <N>` counts are printed
Open Vulnerabilities table includes columns ID, Package, Severity, Status, Priority, Decision
Open vulns are sorted by CWSS priority (P1 first), then by severity
Skill does NOT modify `.vulnetix/memory.yaml` or any other file

evals.prompt: Just onboarded to this repo — what prior security decisions have already been made here?
evals.expected_output: Dashboard rendering with both Open and Resolved tables so the user can see prior triage history and decisions.
expectations: If `.vulnetix/memory.yaml` is missing, output is exactly `No vulnerability data found. Run /vulnetix:vuln <package> or /vulnetix:exploits-search to start tracking.`
Resolved Vulnerabilities table includes columns ID, Package, Severity, Resolution, Decision, Date
Date column uses the most recent `history` entry timestamp with `discovery.date` as fallback
Entries with `decision.choice: risk-accepted` and `decision.choice: deferred` are surfaced under Resolved
Suggested next-action lines reference `/vulnetix:exploits`, `/vulnetix:fix`, or `/vulnetix:remediation` per state

evals.prompt: Pre-release check — any open high-severity items I should worry about before tagging?
evals.expected_output: Dashboard with emphasis on the Open table, sorted by CWSS priority, plus suggested follow-ups for each open vuln.
expectations: Open vulns with `status: under_investigation` and `status: affected` are both classified as Open
Up to 5 suggested next-actions are printed for the top open vulns
Manifest tracking table is rendered with Manifest, Ecosystem, Last Scanned, Vulns Found
Final line always reads `Use /vulnetix:vuln <id> for detailed info on any vulnerability.`
Table is capped at 50 rows when more than 200 vulns are tracked
